20:2: We did not send down the Quran to you that you might fall into distress.
20:3: Except as an admonition for whoever fears.
20:4: A sending down from the One Who created the earth and the high heavens.
20:6: Whatever is in the heavens, whatever is on the earth, whatever is between the two, and whatever is under the soil belongs to Him.
20:7: Even if you speak the word aloud, surely He knows the secret and what is even more hidden.
20:8: Allah, there is no deity except Him, the most beautiful names belong to Him.
20:9: And did the hadith of Moses come to you?
20:10: When he saw a fire and said to his family: 'Wait, I have sensed a fire; perhaps I may bring you an ember from it or find a guide by the fire.'
20:11: So when he came to it, Moses was called to: 'O Moses!'
20:12: Surely I am your Rabb, take off your shoes, for you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
20:13: I have chosen you, so now listen to what is revealed.
20:14: Surely I am Allah, there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish salah for My remembrance.
20:15: Surely the Hour is coming, I almost keep it hidden so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives.
20:16: So let not the one who does not believe in it and follows his desire turn you away from it, lest you perish.
20:17: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
20:18: He said: "It is my staff. I lean upon it, with it I shake down leaves for my sheep, and I have other needs in it as well."
20:20: Thereupon he threw it, and behold, it was a serpent moving swiftly.
20:21: He said: "Take it and do not fear. We will return it to its former state."
20:22: Put your hand into your wing, that it may come out pure white without flaw, as another miracle.
20:23: In order that We may show you of Our greatest signs.
20:24: Go to Pharaoh, surely he has transgressed.
20:25: He said: 'My Rabb, expand for me my breast.'
20:27: Untie the knot from my tongue,
20:28: That they may understand my speech.
20:29: And appoint for me a minister from my family,
20:32: And make him a partner in my task,
20:33: So that we may glorify You much,
20:34: And remember and mention You often.
20:35: Surely You have been seeing us.
20:36: He said: 'O Moses, what you asked for has indeed been granted to you.'
20:37: And indeed, We bestowed favor upon you another time.
20:38: When We revealed to your mother what was revealed.
20:39: 'Put him into the chest, then cast him into the sea so that the sea may cast him onto the shore; an enemy to Me and an enemy to him will take him.' And I cast love upon you from Me, and so that you might be raised under My eye.
20:40: When your sister was walking and saying: 'Shall I point out to you someone who will take care of him?' Thus We returned you to your mother so that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve. And you killed a person, yet We saved you from sorrow and tested you with various trials. You stayed for years among the people of Midian, then you came according to a decree, O Moses.
20:41: I have chosen you for Myself.
20:42: Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in remembering Me.
20:43: Go to Pharaoh, surely he has transgressed.
20:44: Speak to him with gentle speech; perhaps he will take heed or fear.
20:45: They said: 'Our Rabb, surely we fear that he may commit excess against us or transgress.'
20:46: He said: 'Do not fear, surely I am with you both; I hear and I see.'
20:47: Go to him and say: 'Surely we are the messengers of your Rabb, so send the Children of Israel with us and do not torment them. We have certainly brought you a sign from your Rabb. And peace be upon whoever follows the guidance.'
20:48: It has been revealed to us that the punishment is upon whoever denies and turns away.
20:49: He said: "Then who is your Rabb, O Moses?"
20:50: He said: 'Our Rabb is the One Who gave everything its creation, then guided it.'
20:51: He said: 'Then what is the state of the former generations?'
20:52: He said: 'The knowledge of it is in a book with my Rabb. My Rabb neither errs nor forgets.'
20:53: He who made the earth a cradle for you and opened pathways in it for you, and sent down water from the sky; so with it We brought forth pairs of diverse plants.
20:54: Eat and pasture your livestock. Surely in that are signs for possessors of intellect.
20:55: From it We created you, into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth another time.
20:56: And indeed, We showed him all Our signs, but he denied and turned away.
20:57: He said: 'O Moses, have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic?'
20:58: We too will certainly bring you magic like it. So appoint between us and you an appointment which neither we nor you will fail to keep, in an even place.
20:59: He said: 'Your appointment is the day of adornment, and that the people be gathered at mid-morning.'
20:60: Pharaoh turned away, gathered his plot, and then came.
20:61: Moses said to them: 'Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment. And whoever invents a falsehood has failed.'
20:62: Thereupon they disputed their affair among themselves and kept it secret.
20:63: They said: 'Surely these two are magicians; they want to drive you out of your land with their magic and eliminate your most exemplary way.'
20:64: So gather your plot, then come in line; and whoever overcomes today has succeeded.
20:65: They said: 'O Moses! Either you throw, or we will be the first to throw.'
20:66: He said: 'Rather, you throw.' And behold, their ropes and their staffs appeared to him, on account of their magic, as though they were striving.
20:67: Thereupon Moses felt a fear within himself.
20:68: We said: 'Do not fear, surely you are the uppermost.'
20:69: Throw what is in your right hand, that it may swallow what they have made; what they have made is only a magician's trick, and the magician does not prosper wherever he goes.
20:70: So the magicians fell down in prostration; they said: 'We believe in the Rabb of Aaron and Moses.'
20:71: He said: 'Did you believe in him before I gave you permission? Surely he is your chief who taught you magic. I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides and crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. And you will know which of us is more severe and more lasting in punishment.'
20:72: They said: 'We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us and the One Who created us. So decree whatever you are going to decree; you only decree in this worldly life.'
20:73: Surely we have believed in our Rabb so that He may forgive us our sins and the magic you compelled us to perform. Allah is better and more lasting.
20:74: Surely whoever comes to his Rabb as a criminal, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
20:75: And whoever comes to Him as a believer and having done righteous deeds, for those there are high ranks.
20:76: Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein. And that is the reward of whoever purifies himself.
20:77: And indeed, We revealed to Moses: 'Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path in the sea, neither fearing being overtaken nor being anxious.'
20:78: Pharaoh followed them with his armies, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them.
20:79: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide.
20:80: O Children of Israel! By oath, We saved you from your enemy, We promised you on the right side of Tur, and We sent down upon you manna and quails.
20:81: Eat from the clean things We have given you as provision and do not exceed limits in it, lest My wrath descends upon you. And upon whomever My wrath descends, he has indeed fallen.
20:82: Undoubtedly I will surely forgive whoever repents, believes, performs righteous deeds, and then enters the right path.
20:83: And what has driven you to hasten away from your people, O Moses?
20:84: He said: 'They, here they are on my track, and I hastened to You, O my Rabb, so that You may be pleased.'
20:85: He said: 'Undoubtedly We put your people into fitnah after you, and the Samiri led them astray.'
20:86: Moses returned to his people, angry and sorrowful. He said: 'O my people! Did not your Rabb make you a good promise? Or did the covenant seem too long to you, or did you desire that wrath from your Rabb should descend upon you, so you broke the promise you gave me?'
20:87: They said: 'We did not break your promise by our own will, but we were loaded with burdens from the ornaments of the people, so we threw them. Thus did the Samiri also throw.'
20:88: Then he brought out for them a calf having a lowing body; they said: 'This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot.'
20:89: Did they not see that it did not return a word to them, and had no power either to harm or to benefit them?
20:90: And by oath, Aaron had said to them before: 'O my people, you were only put into fitnah with it, and undoubtedly your Rabb is ar-Rahman. Therefore follow me and obey my command.'
20:91: They said: 'We will never cease to remain devoted to worshiping it until Moses returns to us.'
20:92: He said: 'O Aaron! What prevented you, when you saw them going astray,'
20:93: 'From following me? Did you disobey my command?'
20:94: He said: 'O son of my mother! Do not seize my beard nor my head. Undoubtedly I feared that you would say, "You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word."'
20:95: He said: 'What then is your affair, O Samiri?'
20:96: He said: 'I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful from the trace of the messenger and threw it. Thus did my soul prompt me.'
20:97: He said: 'Go! Undoubtedly for you in life is to say, "No touching!" and undoubtedly for you is a promise that you will never fail to keep; and look at your god to which you remained devoted: we will certainly burn it, then we will scatter it into the sea.'
20:98: Your god is only Allah, other than Whom there is no god; He has encompassed all things in knowledge.
20:99: Thus We relate to you from the tidings of what has passed, and We have given you a reminder (dhikr) from Our presence.
20:100: Whoever turns away from it, undoubtedly he will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection.
20:101: They will abide eternally therein; and what an evil burden it is for them on the Day of Resurrection.
20:102: The Day the Sur is blown, on that Day We will gather the criminals with blue-gray eyes.
20:103: They whisper among themselves, saying: "You stayed only ten (days)."
20:104: We know best what they say. At that time the most exemplary of them says: "You stayed only a day."
20:105: And they ask you about the mountains, so say: 'My Rabb will blast them, scattering them as dust.'
20:106: Thus He will leave it as a smooth, level plain.
20:107: You will see in it neither crookedness nor any mound.
20:108: On that Day, they will follow the caller; in him there is no crookedness. Voices are humbled before ar-Rahman, so you hear nothing but a whisper.
20:109: On that Day, intercession does not benefit, except for him whom ar-Rahman permits and with whose word He is pleased.
20:110: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, while they cannot encompass Him in knowledge.
20:111: Faces are humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer (al-Qayyum), and whoever bears injustice has indeed failed.
20:112: Whoever performs righteous deeds while being a believer shall fear neither injustice nor deprivation.
20:113: And thus We sent it down as an Arabic Quran and explained various threats in it, so that perhaps they may beware or it may produce for them a reminder.
20:114: Exalted is Allah, the True King; do not hasten with the Quran before its revelation to you is completed, and say: 'My Rabb, increase me in knowledge.'
20:115: And by oath, We had made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found no resolve in him.
20:116: When We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused.
20:117: Thereupon We said: 'O Adam, undoubtedly this is an enemy to you and your wife. Let him not drive you two out of Paradise, lest you become wretched.'
20:118: Undoubtedly for you is that you will neither go hungry therein nor be naked.
20:119: And you will neither be thirsty therein nor exposed to the sun.
20:120: But Satan whispered to him, saying: "O Adam! Shall I show you the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will not perish?"
20:121: Thereupon they both ate from it, immediately their shameful parts appeared to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of Paradise. Adam disobeyed his Rabb and went astray.
20:122: Then his Rabb chose him, thus accepted his repentance and guided him.
20:123: He said: "Get down from it, all of you together. Some of you will be enemies to others. Then whenever guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor become wretched."
20:124: Whoever turns away from My reminder, undoubtedly for him is a narrow livelihood, and on the Day of Resurrection We will gather him blind.
20:125: He said: 'My Rabb, why have You gathered me blind, while I used to be seeing?'
20:126: He said: 'Thus Our verses came to you, and thus you forgot them; and just like that, today you are forgotten.'
20:127: And thus do We recompense whoever was wasteful and did not believe in the verses of his Rabb. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.
20:128: Did it not guide them, how many generations We destroyed before them, while they walk in their dwellings? Undoubtedly in that are signs for people of understanding.
20:129: And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Rabb and a determined term, the punishment would certainly have been inevitable.
20:130: Be patient over what they say, and glorify with the praise of your Rabb before the rising of the sun and before its setting; and glorify during the hours of the night and at the ends of the day, so that you may be pleased.
20:131: Do not extend your eyes toward what We have granted some pairs among them as the ornament of the life of the world, in order to test them thereby. The provision of your Rabb is better and more enduring.
20:132: Enjoin salah upon your family and patiently persevere in it yourself. We do not ask provision of you; We provide for you. And the outcome is for taqwa.
20:133: They said: "If only he had brought us a sign from his Rabb!" Did there not come to them the clear evidence of what was in the former scriptures?
20:134: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said: "Our Rabb! If only You had sent us a messenger so that we could have followed Your verses before being humiliated and disgraced," they would have said.
20:135: Say: "Everyone is waiting, you too wait. Soon you will know who the owners of the straight path are and who has attained guidance."
